quickSummary: Discovered by Sir Hans Krebs in 1937, the TCA (Citric Acid) cycle oxidizes Acetyl-CoA (2C) by condensing it with Oxaloacetate (4C) in the mitochondrial matrix to form Citrate (6C). Through 8 enzymatic steps, 2 CO₂ molecules are released, generating 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂, and 1 GTP/ATP per turn. Succinate Dehydrogenase (Step 6) is the only membrane-bound TCA enzyme (Complex II). For 1 glucose molecule (2 turns), the net yield is 6 NADH + 2 FADH₂ + 2 GTP (ATP) + 4 CO₂.

conceptBreakdown.content:
The Tricarboxylic Acid (TCA) cycle (Krebs Cycle / Citric Acid Cycle) is the central catabolic hub located inside the **Mitochondrial Matrix** that completes the oxidation of carbon from carbohydrate, fat, and protein degradation.

- **Initiation**: Acetyl-CoA ($2\text{C}$) condenses with Oxaloacetic acid (OAA, $4\text{C}$) to form Citric acid ($6\text{C}$), catalyzed by **Citrate Synthase** with the consumption of $1\text{ H}_2\text{O}$.
- **Two Oxidative Decarboxylations**:
  1. **Isocitrate Dehydrogenase**: Converts Isocitrate ($6\text{C}$) to $\alpha$-Ketoglutarate ($5\text{C}$), releasing the first $\text{CO}_2$ and $1\text{ NADH}$.
  2. **$\alpha$-Ketoglutarate Dehydrogenase**: Converts $\alpha$-KG ($5\text{C}$) to Succinyl-CoA ($4\text{C}$), releasing the second $\text{CO}_2$ and generating $1\text{ NADH}$.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### Step-by-Step Enzymatic Inventory of the Krebs Cycle

| Step | Enzyme | Substrate $\rightarrow$ Product | High-Yield Energy / By-product |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **Citrate Synthase** | Acetyl-$\text{CoA}$ ($2\text{C}$) + $\text{OAA}$ ($4\text{C}$) $\rightarrow$ Citrate ($6\text{C}$) | Consumes $1\text{ H}_2\text{O}$; releases $\text{CoA-SH}$ |
| **2** | Aconitase | Citrate $\rightleftharpoons$ cis-Aconitate $\rightleftharpoons$ Isocitrate ($6\text{C}$) | Dehydration followed by rehydration |
| **3** | **Isocitrate Dehydrogenase** | Isocitrate ($6\text{C}$) $\rightarrow$ $\alpha$-Ketoglutarate ($5\text{C}$) | **1st $\text{CO}_2$ released**; **Generates $1\text{ NADH}$** |
| **4** | **$\alpha$-Ketoglutarate Dehydrogenase** | $\alpha$-Ketoglutarate ($5\text{C}$) $\rightarrow$ Succinyl-$\text{CoA}$ ($4\text{C}$) | **2nd $\text{CO}_2$ released**; **Generates $1\text{ NADH}$** |
| **5** | **Succinyl-CoA Synthetase** | Succinyl-$\text{CoA}$ ($4\text{C}$) $\rightarrow$ Succinate ($4\text{C}$) | **Substrate-Level Phosphorylation ($1\text{ GTP/ATP}$)** |
| **6** | **Succinate Dehydrogenase** | Succinate ($4\text{C}$) $\rightarrow$ Fumarate ($4\text{C}$) | **Generates $1\text{ FADH}_2$** *(Bound to Inner Membrane as Complex II)* |
| **7** | Fumarase | Fumarate ($4\text{C}$) $\rightarrow$ L-Malate ($4\text{C}$) | Hydration reaction (adds $\text{H}_2\text{O}$) |
| **8** | **Malate Dehydrogenase** | L-Malate ($4\text{C}$) $\rightarrow$ Oxaloacetate ($4\text{C}$) | **Generates $1\text{ NADH}$** |

$$\mathbf{\text{Net TCA Yield per Glucose (2 Turns): 2 Acetyl-CoA} \longrightarrow 6\text{ NADH} + 2\text{ FADH}_2 + 2\text{ GTP (ATP)} + 4\text{ CO}_2\uparrow}$$
